questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Chain Rule
questions.worked_solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $arctan$ and $arcsec$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arctanx) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(arcsec({x}^{2}))) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec({x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(arcsec({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}(1+{arcsec}^{2}({x}^{2}))}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arcsec$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2arcsec(6x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec(6x-1)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|6x-1|\sqrt{(6x-1)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x-1) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|6x-1|\sqrt{{(6x-1)}^{2}-1}}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{12}{|6x-1|\sqrt{36{x}^{2}-12x}} \\  & =\frac{12}{|6x-1|\sqrt{4(9{x}^{2}-3x)}} \\  & =\frac{6}{|6x-1|\sqrt{9{x}^{2}-3x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Product Rule
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccot$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}\cdot arccot(\sqrt{x})) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})\cdot arccot(\sqrt{x})+\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,(\sqrt{x})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\cdot arccot(\sqrt{x})+\sqrt{x}\cdot [-\frac{1}{1+{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})] \\  & =\frac{arccot(\sqrt{x})}{2\sqrt{x}}-\frac{\sqrt{x}}{1+x}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{arccot(\sqrt{x})}{2\sqrt{x}}-\frac{1}{2(1+x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Product Rule
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccot$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{4}⁡x\cdot arccot\,x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{4}⁡x)\cdot arccot\,x+{log}_{4}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\cdot arccot\,x+{log}_{4}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{arccot\,x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{1+{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Quotient Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we let $u(x)={3}^{x}$ and $v(x)=arccsc\,x,$ and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)\cdot arccsc\,x-{3}^{x}\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})}{{(arccsc\,x)}^{2}}. \\  & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{arccsc\,x}{{(arccsc\,x)}^{2}}+\frac{{3}^{x}}{{(arccsc\,x)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}} \\  & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\frac{1}{arccsc\,x}+\frac{{3}^{x}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\frac{1}{|x|{(arccsc\,x)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
